exception: A French loanword (counterpart) that keeps the neuter gender; it is not a person noun like the der words in -ant.
A person noun (consumer) built with the Latin ending -ent; like other person nouns it is masculine. It only looks like a -ment word.
'Concern' ends in -nis but is feminine; it belongs to the feminine minority in this group like die Kenntnis.
'Darkness' ends in -nis but is feminine like die Wildnis.
'Gloom' (as in Trübsal blasen) ends in -sal but is feminine unlike das Schicksal.
'Obedience' is masculine and not neuter despite the Ge- prefix.
'Form' or 'figure' is feminine despite the Ge- prefix.
'Renunciation' is masculine because it is the noun of the verb verzichten (der Verzicht auf etwas); it is not one of the neuter -icht words like das Licht.
'Confidence' is one of the -sicht nouns and stays feminine like die Sicht.
Means deadline, a short native word and not a person, so the -ist person rule doesn't apply.
A one-syllable word (haste) like die Last; the rule is for longer -ast nouns.
An English loanword (public image) that ends in -age only in spelling; it is pronounced the English way and is neuter.
A word for a person (nomad) and therefore masculine like other male person nouns; a woman is die Nomadin.
